feature.name: Alliance Treasure Hunt
feature.summary: A 72-hour weekly alliance event: members earn Map Fragments from battles and daily quests, exchange ten fragments for a Treasure Chest, and unlock shared milestone rewards at 100, 250 and 500 opened chests. The design sets three measurable criteria: 40% of eligible alliances start a hunt, non-participants' day-7 retention does not drop, and Fragment Packs stay below 15% of fragments earned.

new_events.name: treasure_hunt_started
new_events.description: An alliance leader starts a Treasure Hunt for the alliance.
new_events.trigger: The server confirms the 500 Ember Coins entry cost was taken from the alliance vault and the hunt is created.
new_events.rationale: The start is the numerator of the first success criterion (40% of eligible alliances start a hunt) and the anchor for every other hunt event.

evidence.quote: An alliance leader starts a hunt by paying an entry cost of 500 Ember Coins from the alliance vault.

properties.name: player_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the acting player.
properties.rationale: Ties the event to a player, as on every existing event.

properties.name: alliance_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the alliance.
properties.rationale: Lets every hunt metric be cut by alliance; same name and type as in alliance_joined.

properties.name: hunt_id
properties.description: Id of one hunt of one alliance.
properties.rationale: Joins all events of a hunt together; a hunt is the unit the success criteria are measured on.

properties.name: alliance_size
properties.description: Members of the alliance at the start.
properties.rationale: Eligibility is five members or more; the size also explains differences in progress speed.

properties.name: entry_cost
properties.description: Ember Coins paid from the vault.
properties.rationale: Keeps the metric valid if the entry cost is ever changed or tested.

new_events.name: treasure_hunt_screen_viewed
new_events.description: A player opens the hunt screen.
new_events.trigger: The hunt screen is shown to the player.
new_events.rationale: The first success criterion needs a denominator: how many eligible alliances were exposed to the event and did not start. Views by leaders versus other members show whether leaders found the feature.

properties.name: player_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the acting player.
properties.rationale: Ties the event to a player, as on every existing event.

properties.name: alliance_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the alliance.
properties.rationale: Lets every hunt metric be cut by alliance; same name and type as in alliance_joined.

properties.name: is_leader
properties.description: Whether the viewer is the alliance leader.
properties.rationale: Only leaders can start a hunt, so views are read separately for them.

properties.name: hunt_active
properties.description: Whether the alliance has a running hunt.
properties.rationale: Separates browsing a running hunt from looking at the start option.

new_events.name: map_fragment_earned
new_events.trigger: The server credits Map Fragments to the player.
new_events.rationale: Fragment inflow shows participation and pace, and its split by source gives the Fragment Pack share (below 15%) directly.

evidence.quote: Members earn Map Fragments from battles and daily quests.

properties.name: player_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the acting player.
properties.rationale: Ties the event to a player, as on every existing event.

properties.name: hunt_id
properties.description: Id of one hunt of one alliance.
properties.rationale: Joins all events of a hunt together; a hunt is the unit the success criteria are measured on.

properties.name: source
properties.description: Where the fragments came from.
properties.rationale: The Fragment Pack criterion is the share of fragments with source pack.

properties.name: amount
properties.description: Fragments credited.
properties.rationale: Pace of the hunt and size of each source.

new_events.name: treasure_chest_opened
new_events.description: A player exchanges ten Map Fragments and opens a Treasure Chest.
new_events.trigger: The chest-opening animation completes and the reward is granted.
new_events.rationale: Chests opened drive the milestones and show how far each hunt gets. Tier and reward show what the event adds to the economy.

evidence.quote: Players open chests after collecting ten map fragments.

properties.name: player_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the acting player.
properties.rationale: Ties the event to a player, as on every existing event.

properties.name: hunt_id
properties.description: Id of one hunt of one alliance.
properties.rationale: Joins all events of a hunt together; a hunt is the unit the success criteria are measured on.

properties.name: chestTier
properties.description: Tier of the chest.
properties.rationale: Tier depends on alliance rank, so it is the economy lever to monitor.

properties.name: reward_type
properties.description: What the chest contained.
properties.rationale: Shows which currencies the event injects into the economy.

properties.name: reward_amount
properties.description: Whole units of the reward.
properties.rationale: Size of the economy injection.

new_events.name: treasure_milestone_reached
new_events.description: An alliance reaches a chest milestone.
new_events.trigger: The server records the 100th, 250th or 500th opened chest of the hunt.
new_events.rationale: Milestones are the event's shared goal; reaching them is the completion measure of a hunt and the moment the milestone push goes out.

evidence.quote: When the alliance reaches 100, 250 and 500 opened chests, every member receives a milestone reward.

properties.name: player_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the acting player.
properties.rationale: Ties the event to a player, as on every existing event.

properties.name: alliance_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the alliance.
properties.rationale: Lets every hunt metric be cut by alliance; same name and type as in alliance_joined.

properties.name: hunt_id
properties.description: Id of one hunt of one alliance.
properties.rationale: Joins all events of a hunt together; a hunt is the unit the success criteria are measured on.

properties.name: milestone
properties.description: Chest count of the milestone: 100, 250 or 500.
properties.rationale: Separates the three completion levels.

new_events.name: treasure_share_forfeited
new_events.description: A member loses their share of a milestone reward by leaving the alliance early.
new_events.trigger: The server withholds a milestone reward because the member left within two hours of the milestone.
new_events.rationale: Shows whether the forfeit rule is hit often, which would signal friction or abuse; alliance_left alone cannot tell when the leave cost a reward.

evidence.quote: Members who leave the alliance within two hours of a milestone forfeit their share of that milestone reward.

properties.description: Opaque id of the acting player.
properties.rationale: Ties the event to a player, as on every existing event.

properties.name: alliance_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the alliance.
properties.rationale: Lets every hunt metric be cut by alliance; same name and type as in alliance_joined.

properties.name: hunt_id
properties.description: Id of one hunt of one alliance.
properties.rationale: Joins all events of a hunt together; a hunt is the unit the success criteria are measured on.

properties.name: milestone
properties.description: Milestone whose reward was forfeited.
properties.rationale: Which milestone members leave around.

properties.name: player_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the acting player.
properties.rationale: Ties the event to a player, as on every existing event.

properties.name: alliance_id
properties.description: Opaque id of the alliance.
properties.rationale: Lets every hunt metric be cut by alliance; same name and type as in alliance_joined.

extended_events.name: purchase_completed
extended_events.rationale: Fragment Pack revenue has to be separable from other purchases, and tied to a hunt, to read the monetisation side of the event.

evidence.quote: Players can buy Fragment Packs for real money, limited to three per day.

add_properties.name: hunt_id
add_properties.description: Hunt the purchase was made for; empty for other purchases.
add_properties.rationale: Links a purchase to a hunt so pack revenue and pack share can be computed per hunt.

reused_events.name: currency_spent
reused_events.rationale: The entry cost is an Ember Coins sink and is already captured here. Agree the sink value treasure_hunt_entry so it can be filtered.

reused_events.name: push_opened
reused_events.rationale: Opens of the milestone push are already captured with campaign_id. Agree a campaign id for hunt milestones.

reused_events.name: alliance_joined
reused_events.rationale: Gives alliance size over time, which defines which alliances are eligible.

reused_events.name: session_started
reused_events.rationale: Day-7 retention of non-participants is read from sessions; no change required.

metrics.name: hunt_start_rate_eligible_alliances
metrics.definition: Share of alliances with five or more members that start a hunt in the first month.

metrics.name: hunt_funnel
metrics.definition: Per hunt: started, fragments earned, chests opened, milestones reached.

metrics.name: fragment_pack_share
metrics.definition: Fragments earned from packs divided by all fragments earned.

metrics.name: non_participant_d7_retention
metrics.definition: Day-7 retention of players in eligible alliances who earned no fragments, against a comparable baseline.
metrics.rationale: Second success criterion: the event must not hurt players who skip it.

metrics.name: early_leave_forfeit_rate
metrics.definition: Forfeited shares divided by milestone rewards granted.
metrics.rationale: Checks the leave rule for friction and abuse.

metrics.name: event_economy_injection
metrics.definition: Currency granted by chests per hunt, against the entry cost sink.

not_tracked.what: One event per Map Fragment drop inside battles.
not_tracked.why: High volume and no extra question answered: fragments are summed per source in map_fragment_earned.
reward_type and reward_amount answer the economy question without a new event per item.

not_tracked.what: Views of the member contribution list.
not_tracked.why: The design leaves its visibility undecided; add it when the question exists.

assumptions: hunt_id is generated by the server when the hunt is created and is stable for its 72 hours.
Only one hunt can run per alliance at a time, as the document states, so hunt_id is unique per alliance and week.
Ember Coins corresponds to the value ember_coins of currency_spent.currency.
open_questions: Should chest contents be allowed to raise battle power? If yes, battle_finished needs a chest-bonus property.
What exactly makes an alliance eligible on Monday (member count at unlock, or at start)?
In which time zone does the Monday unlock happen? It decides how days are cut in the funnel.
